additional_concerns: The candidate's allocation, actual-authority and consistent-conduct test is an interpretive proposal, not an express sufficiency test in paragraph 10. Whether supervisory discharge is required remains unresolved; neither formal allocation alone nor a service failure alone settles retained accountability.
No arrangement-specific facts establish actual retention or discharge of responsibility. Missing standards or facts must remain unresolved rather than produce a false result.

Paragraph 14 places the request condition expressly on demonstration and requires demonstration to the SFC's satisfaction. Footnote 5 supplies minimum content; its independent wording also leaves a rival unqualified-demonstration reading to resolve. Absence of a request does not remove confirmation or underlying responsibility.
Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Neither procurement establishes fulfillment of paragraph 10.

Intermediary paragraphs 17–18 impose activity-specific due diligence and controls expectations. Their applicability and the missing Appendix factors require assessment before importing them into this Product Provider control.
The source does not require personal performance of every delegated task or reservation of every operational decision. Conversely, permissible delegation does not establish adequate supervision.
No executable meaning is supplied. The reported structural check and retrieval results establish neither legal sufficiency nor correspondence.
